title: The Vector of Kepler Reach
premise: Edmund Yarrow, sole caretaker of the derelict Kepler Reach seed vault, answers a distress signal broadcast in a language dead for two centuries — and discovers the vault's original crew, cryo-frozen and waking, whose existence both fleets in orbit would kill to control. Posing as the vault's legitimate inheritor, she fabricates a chain of custody that keeps the rival fleets at bay while she helps the sleepers choose their own future. When her forgery unravels, Edmund must broadcast the truth in the extinct language she has secretly spent years learning, forcing both fleets to stand down as the vault's failing reactor counts toward detonation. The novel ends with the sleepers granted sovereignty over Kepler Reach, Edmund formally adopted into their line, and her cargo hauler rechristened as the vault's first supply ship.
about_author: Beatrix Ishikawa is a former orbital logistics dispatcher who turned to fiction after twenty years of listening to pilots talk their way through impossible situations. She writes about people who keep things running when no one is watching.

chapters.title: Cold Cargo
chapters.summary: Edmund Yarrow's POV. Edmund makes her quarterly supply run to the abandoned Kepler Reach seed vault, cataloguing frost damage and talking to the empty corridors out of habit. The chapter establishes her loneliness, her debt to the Meridian Cartel, and her strange fluency in the dead Vessian language. Emotional beat: quiet devotion to a forgotten place.

chapters.title: A Voice in Dead Tongues
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. A distress signal arrives in Vessian — precise, grammatical, alive. Edmund verifies it isn't a pirate lure and traces it to the vault's sealed cryogenic deck, a level officially decommissioned before her tenure. She breaks protocol and descends. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into dread.

chapters.title: The Sleepers of Deck Nine
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Behind a jammed blast door she finds twelve intact cryopods — the vault's original crew, presumed dead for two centuries. One pod is failing: a woman named Ilse Varga, whose vitals triggered the signal. Edmund faces an impossible choice: report the discovery and lose them to whoever claims salvage rights, or hide them. Emotional beat: awe and fear of responsibility.

chapters.title: Inheritance of Strangers
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV, waking. Ilse surfaces from cryo disoriented, two hundred years displaced, and finds a stranger speaking her mother tongue. Through halting conversation, Edmund learns the vault was never abandoned — its crew was deliberately erased from records by a corporate purge. Emotional beat: grief for a stolen century.

chapters.title: Two Fleets at the Door
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. The Meridian Cartel and the Concordat Navy both detect anomalous power readings from Kepler Reach and dispatch ships. Edmund, panicking, fabricates a succession certificate naming herself heir to the vault's original charter. Emotional beat: the lie begins, half desperation, half resolve.

chapters.title: The Cartel's Auditor
chapters.summary: Dario Senn's POV. Cartel auditor Dario Senn docks to inspect Edmund's claim, all charm and hidden ledgers. He finds her paperwork flawless — too flawless — but the vault's reactor fault forces him to treat her as a partner in crisis rather than a suspect. Emotional beat: cat-and-mouse with mutual grudging respect.

chapters.title: What the Seeds Remember
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Ilse and the waking crew explore the vault, finding their own names carved into germination records and crops grown from their stored seeds by generations of caretakers — including Edmund's grandmother. Ilse realizes Edmund is heir to a promise, not just a building. Emotional beat: found family taking root.

chapters.title: Countdown in the Walls
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. The reactor's containment fault proves worse than reported: an uncontrolled cascade will breach in roughly three weeks. Edmund must evacuate the sleepers or repair systems designed by people two centuries dead. She chooses repair, enlisting Ilse, who helped build the vault. Emotional beat: determination against the clock.

chapters.title: The Concordat's Offer
chapters.summary: Captain Rehn's POV. Concordat Captain Rehn arrives with a diplomatic offer: legitimate sovereignty papers for the vault's heirs — if the sleepers' cryotechnology is surrendered to Navy research. Edmund stalls, buying time while concealing that the 'heirs' are awake and watching from the gallery. Emotional beat: temptation and the price of legitimacy.

chapters.title: Lessons for the Living
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Ilse teaches Edmund the formal registers of Vessian needed to authenticate her forged charter, and in the process learns how Edmund taught herself the language from salvaged children's readers. Ilse names Edmund her sworn daughter before witnesses. Emotional beat: inheritance freely given, versus inheritance forged.

chapters.title: Senn's Ledger
chapters.summary: Dario's POV. Dario cross-references the charter's seal against Cartel archives and finds the forgery — but also finds the original purge order that erased the crew, signed by his own cartel's founders. He sits on the evidence, torn between duty and conscience. Emotional beat: complicity across generations.

chapters.title: Thirteen Days
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. With the cascade accelerating, Edmund runs repair shifts with the waking crew while juggling both fleets' demands. A near-fatal coolant burn leaves her burned and shaken; Ilse takes the watch over her. Emotional beat: the caretaker learning to be cared for.

chapters.title: The Salvage Claim
chapters.summary: Captain Rehn's POV. Rehn, pressured by Navy command, files a salvage claim on the vault, voiding Edmund's charter. Dario, seeing his opening, counters with the Cartel's own claim — and privately warns Edmund that both sides will seize the sleepers as 'assets' once the reactor is stabilized. Emotional beat: allies becoming adversaries.

chapters.title: What Ilse Built
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Ilse reveals the vault's hidden design: a manual shutdown protocol she and the original crew installed, reachable only through the Vessian interface — untranslatable to either fleet. The catch: it requires three crew members working in synchrony for eleven hours, inside the failing reactor shield. Emotional beat: hope with a terrible cost.

chapters.title: The Lie That Holds
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Edmund plays both fleets against each other, feeding each a version of the truth: the reactor will breach and take the vault's irreplaceable genetic archive with it unless their crews stand down and cooperate on evacuation. The bluff works — barely — and a fragile joint operation forms. Emotional beat: the liar becoming the only honest broker.

chapters.title: Breach Warning
chapters.summary: Dario's POV. During the joint operation, a Concordat officer discovers the sleepers' pods and broadcasts it fleet-wide. Both fleets mobilize to seize them; the countdown drops to four days as the cascade accelerates from the power surges. Dario must choose sides publicly. Emotional beat: the lie collapses.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Edmund seizes the vault's transmitter and broadcasts in fluent Vessian — the language of the charter both fleets claim to honor — declaring the crew alive, sovereign, and the rightful heirs, with Dario authenticating the original purge order as proof of the fleets' illegitimate claims. The broadcast buys hours, not peace. Emotional beat: truth as a weapon.

chapters.title: Eleven Hours
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Ilse, Edmund, and crew engineer Tam Osei enter the reactor shield to run the shutdown protocol while the fleets' standoff turns into scattered skirmishes outside. The sequence is grueling; Tam's suit fails near the end and Ilse holds the synchrony alone for the final hour. Emotional beat: sacrifice and trust under fire.

chapters.title: Zero Hour
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. The cascade stalls at ninety seconds to breach — the protocol works, but the vault is crippled and dark. Edmund, injured, drags herself to the transmitter to confirm the fleets have stood down: Rehn, shamed by the purge evidence, withdraws; the Cartel, exposed by Dario, negotiates. Emotional beat: exhaustion after survival.

chapters.title: Terms of the Living
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Negotiations conclude: the sleepers receive legal sovereignty over Kepler Reach under a restored charter, with Edmund recognized as sworn heir and Dario as neutral registrar. Ilse must decide whether to wake the remaining pods — and chooses yes, all of them. Emotional beat: a future chosen deliberately.

chapters.title: The Vector of Kepler Reach
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Edmund rechristens her battered hauler as the vault's first supply ship, her route now a lifeline instead of a lonely circuit. She plants the season's first seeds in the restored bay with Ilse beside her. Emotional beat: homecoming to a place that was never empty.

chapters.title: Charter Day
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV, brief passages from Edmund, Ilse, and Dario. One year later, the vault hosts its first Charter Day: crops in the bays, children of the woken crew learning two centuries of history, and Edmund signing the register as heir — her name written in Vessian, freely given this time. The last line echoes the distress signal that began it all, now a greeting. Emotional beat: belonging, earned and permanent.
